up.

### G5 — the `Pool` is not separated from its `Arena` (opened)

**Origin.** VERIFY-033 F4 recorded this reading as a hypothesis for a later
arc: `pool_reset_reset_ensures_part3` (`pool->used == 0`) "fails because
nothing separates `*pool` from the `*arena` the call havocs", and
`pool_init`'s four `ensures` goals "read the same way". The argument blocks
still file those goals under arithmetic (pool Cat 2a) and delegation (pool
Cat 2d). Re-reading both blocks for entry 2's conjunct brought the
hypothesis back, and G5 takes it up.

**Finding.** `pool_init` requires `\valid(pool)` and `arena_invariant(arena)`
and, since the G4 pool repair, that the `Pool` lie outside the arena's free
tail. `pool_invariant` states `\valid(p)` and `arena_invariant(p->arena)`.
Nothing separates `*pool` from `*arena`, so a `Pool` that overlaps its
`Arena` is admitted.

In C the overlap reaches `pool_init`'s first postcondition. `pool_init`
stores the `Pool`'s first four fields, calls `arena_alloc`, then stores
`base_mark` and `end_mark`. `tools/probes/verify-039/p_pool_arena.c` places
the `Arena` at the `Pool`'s `base_mark` field in one heap block, so that
`base_mark` and `end_mark` are the bytes of the `Arena`'s `buffer` and
`capacity`. The first four stores miss the `Arena`, `arena_alloc` runs on it
intact, and the last two overwrite `buffer` with the region's offset, 0, and
`capacity` with the arena's new offset. `pool_init` returns true, and its
second and third postconditions hold. The `Arena` it was given can no longer
be used: its `buffer` field holds bytes stored as a `usize`, and the next
read of that field through its own type is undefined (C11 6.5p7; G4's scope
calls this the undefined step). Read as bytes, through `memcpy`, the field
is a null pointer, and on that reading the first postcondition,
`pool_invariant(pool)`, is false. The library and the probe make no
undefined access: the block is heap storage, each field the library reads
after a `Pool` store was last stored with a compatible type, and the probe
reads the overwritten fields only through `memcpy` and `memcmp`. The result
is the same in both build configurations, at LP64 and ILP32, with gcc and
clang at `-O0` and `-O2`, and the sanitizers are clean. No placement we
found reaches the fields of the other four goals below without such a read
inside the library: each overlap that reaches them makes the library read an
`Arena` or `Pool` field last stored through a field of another type.

WP leaves the first postcondition unproved. Its goal is pool Cat 2a's
goal 1, `pool_init_ensures_part4`, filed under arithmetic. Cat 2a's argument
derives the arithmetic conjunct "by construction", and the arena repair's
coverage update rests the `arena_invariant(p->arena)` part on
`arena_alloc`'s postcondition, presuming that nothing before the call
changes the `Arena`. Neither covers the two stores after the call, the ones
the probe uses: for goal 1 the argument is defective as written. In WP's
typed model the two structs' `usize` fields share one memory array and
their pointer fields another, so without the separation a store into either
may change the other, and a call that assigns `*arena` may change the
`Pool`. The other four goals VERIFY-033 F4 named state no arithmetic at all:

| Goal | Statement | Filed under |
|---|---|---|
| `pool_init_ensures_2_part4` | `pool->used == 0` | pool Cat 2a, goal 2 (arithmetic) |
| `pool_init_ensures_3_part4` | `pool->capacity == max_objects` | pool Cat 2a, goal 3 (arithmetic) |
| `pool_init_ensures_4_part3` | on failure, `arena->offset == \old(arena->offset)` | pool Cat 2a, goal 4 (arithmetic) |
| `pool_reset_reset_ensures_part3` | `pool->used == 0` | pool Cat 2d, goal 3 (delegation) |

Cat 2d's root-cause bullet describes `reset_ensures_part3` as the
re-establishment of `pool_invariant`; that is `reset_ensures_2_part3`, and
`reset_ensures_part3` is `pool->used == 0`.

Each states a field the function stores, or one it must leave as it found
it, across stores into the other struct or a call that assigns `*arena`:
`pool_init` stores four `Pool` fields before `arena_alloc`, and `pool_reset`
stores `used` before it. The missing separation suffices to explain all
four, and the arithmetic the record names explains none; whether adding it
closes them is the repair's prediction. Cat 2a's own note already doubts the
classification of the `ensures_part4` goals (LIMITATION-SUSPECTED). This is
G1's shape: a separation the contract lacks, goals unproved and misfiled,
and one of them not true for an admitted call.

**Repair (recommended, next).** `pool_init` gains
`requires \separated(pool, arena);` and `pool_invariant` the conjunct
`\separated(p, p->arena)`, so every function that takes the invariant has
it. The prediction will say which of the goals above close, and whether
`pool_init_call_arena_alloc_requires`, `pool_reset_call_arena_alloc_requires`
and `pool_reset_reset_ensures_2_part3`, which state `arena_invariant` or
`pool_invariant` across the same stores, go with them. One intervention per
prediction: it follows the runner pin's scoring.

### G4 — listing, entry 3: a `Bitset` whose fields lie in its own words

**Finding.** `bitset_mut`, and `bitset_view` within it, does not separate
`*bs` from `bs->words`. `bitset_init` requires the separation, but
`bitset_clear_all` and `bitset_set_all` require only `bitset_mut(bs)`, so
they admit a `Bitset` built otherwise, with its fields inside the words it
manages. Both write the words through `char *`: `bitset_clear_all` with
`mem_zero`, and `bitset_set_all` with `mem_set` before it calls
`bitset_clear_padding`, which requires `bitset_mut(bs)`. Three goals that WP
proves in `frama-c-bitset` are false when the write covers the `Bitset`:

| Function | Goals false when the write covers `*bs` |
|---|---|
| `bitset_clear_all` | `ensures bitset_mut(bs)` |
| `bitset_set_all` | at its call to `bitset_clear_padding`, `requires bitset_mut(bs)`; its own `ensures bitset_mut(bs)` |

None is among the residuals. `tools/probes/verify-039/p_bitset_self.c`
places the `Bitset` at the start of a heap block, with its words starting at
its `word_count` field, so that `word_count` lies in `words[0]`. With
capacity 128, two words, `bitset_mut` holds before each call.
`bitset_clear_all` leaves `word_count` at 0 and `bitset_set_all` at all
ones. The capacity is a multiple of 64, so `bitset_clear_padding` writes
nothing, and the state after `bitset_set_all` is the state at that call.
`bitset_mut` is VIOLATED at all three points. The result is the same in
both build configurations, at LP64 and ILP32, with gcc and clang at `-O0`
and `-O2`, and the sanitizers are clean. The block is heap storage, the
clobbering writes are character-type writes, and nothing reads `words[0]`
as a `u64`.

**Decision (recommended).** `bitset_mut` gains
`\separated(bs, bs->words + (0 .. bs->word_count - 1))`, which `bitset_init`
already establishes. The same separation bears on G6.

### G4 — listing, entry 4: `diag_render` into a buffer that covers the `Diag`

**Finding.** `diag_render` requires `d` readable with `diag_invariant(*d)`
and `buf` valid for `buf_size` bytes, and does not separate the two. It
writes through `char *`: `buf[0] = '\0'`, then `snprintf` at `buf + total`,
which on the first iteration is `buf` itself, under the trusted axiom whose
`assigns` is `((char *)buf)[0 .. size - 1]`. In the model those writes
cannot reach `d->depth`, a `usize`, so the loop invariant
`render_i_bounds`, `0 <= i <= d->depth`, proves preserved, and none of
`diag_render`'s goals is among the residuals.
`tools/probes/verify-039/p_diag_render.c` gives a `Diag` two frames and
points `buf` into it at the last frame's message, unused, with `buf_size`
running to the end of `depth`. `buf` is derived from `(char *)&d`, so it
ranges over the `Diag`'s bytes (C11 6.3.2.3p7). A pointer derived from the
`message` member could not go past it, and gcc at `_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3`
aborts one that tries; level 2, and clang, do not. Frame 0's message is
sized so that its rendered line is exactly as long as the distance from
`buf` to `depth`. `snprintf`'s terminating `'\0'` then lands on `depth`'s
first byte, its low byte on the project's little-endian targets, and
`depth` goes from 2 to 0. The loop has run once, so at its next head `i` is
1 and `depth` is 0: the invariant is false there, and the loop exits after
one frame of two. `diag_render`'s own postcondition holds. The result is the
same in both build configurations, at LP64 and ILP32, with gcc and clang at
`-O0`, `-O2` and `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3`, and the sanitizers are clean. The
`Diag` is a declared object, every write into it from `buf` is a
character-type write, `depth` is read back through its declared type, and
the rendered line overlaps none of `snprintf`'s string arguments.

This goal is not a postcondition: it is a step of the proof, false while
the contract's own clauses hold. G4 concerns goals, and this one is proved
and false.

**Decision (recommended).** `diag_render` gains a precondition separating
`buf + (0 .. buf_size - 1)` from `*d`, guarded like `r_buf`.
`diag_render_frame` writes through `char *` with `buf` likewise unseparated
from `*f`, but no goal reads `*f` after its writes, so it is not an entry.

### G4 — listing, entry 5: a vec in its own items

**Finding.** The vec contracts require `*v` readable and writable and
`v->items` valid up to `capacity`, and do not separate the two. That holds
for `frama-c-vec`'s driver predicates, `vec_int_view` and `vec_int_mut`, and
for the inlined first `requires` of the macro-body contracts the `-CC` units
verify. Two placements falsify goals that WP proves.

*In the free tail.* `append_array` copies the new elements with
`mem_copy`, through `char *`, and its ensures 3,
`\forall k < \old(v->len): v->items[k] == \old(v->items[k])`, proves; of its
ensures only the fourth is among the residuals.
`tools/probes/verify-039/p_vec_append_self.c` places a `vec_int` at
`items[len]`, the first free slot, so the copy overwrites its `items` field.
The two "ints" appended are the bytes of a pointer to another array, stored
there as an `int *`. The copy gives the overwritten bytes the effective type
of their source, so after the call `v->items` reads, through its own type,
as a pointer to that array, and ensures 3 compares it with the old
elements: VIOLATED. `append_array` stores `v->len` again after the copy, so
ensures 1 and 2 hold, and it reads no element of `src` as an `int`. Both
build configurations, LP64 and ILP32, gcc and clang at `-O0`, `-O2` and
`-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3`; sanitizers clean. This is the `vec_int` of
`frama-c-vec` and `cc-vec`. At this placement `insert` with `i < len`
moves elements up to `items[len]`, the start of the vec's `items` field,
which `v->items[i] = item` then reads: that call is undefined. With
`i == len`, and in `push`, `try_push` and `push_unchecked`, the element
store itself lands on the `items` field: a typed store over a pointer,
G5's case. `remove`'s move, over `items[i .. len - 2]`, never reaches the
vec.

*In its live elements, where `len` is a `Rec`'s `due`.* `cc-vec_struct`
verifies `vec_Rec`, with `Rec` = `struct { u32 id; i64 due; }`. In the
x86_64 machdep, and with glibc on LP64, a `vec_Rec` placed at `items[0]` has
its `len` field exactly where `Rec[0].due` is: a `usize` (`unsigned long`)
over an `i64` (`long`), signed and unsigned counterparts, which the model
keeps in two arrays. Every store the library makes to
`v->len` then changes `Rec[0]`, an element the frames say is unchanged.
`tools/probes/verify-039/p_vec_rec_live.c` makes seven calls, each on a
fresh vec, and reads `Rec[0].due` through a plain `i64` lvalue, the
counterpart of the `usize` stored there, and through `memcpy`; seven goals
are VIOLATED, none among the residuals:

| Call | Goal |
|---|---|
| `insert(v, 2, item)` at `len` 2 | ensures 4, `items[k]` unchanged for `k < i` |
| `remove(v, 2, &out)` at `len` 3 | ensures 4, the same |
| `push`, `try_push` at `len` 2 | ensures 4, `items[k]` unchanged for `k < \old(len)` |
| `push_unchecked` at `len` 2 | ensures 3, the same |
| `pop(v, &out)` at `len` 3 | ensures 4, `items[k]` unchanged for `k < len` |
| `append_array(v, src, 2)` at `len` 2 | ensures 3, `items[k]` unchanged for `k < \old(len)` |

The vec's `items` field lies over `Rec[0].id` and its padding, and its
`capacity` over `Rec[1]`'s; the library reads them through their own types
and stores no element there, so every access is defined. Both build
configurations, gcc and clang at `-O0`, `-O2` and `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3`,
sanitizers clean. On ILP32 `len` is four bytes and covers only half of
`due`, and the probe says so.
At `vec_int` the same placement changes `int` elements through a `usize`
store. Reading them through their own type afterwards is the undefined step
of G4's scope, so G4 does not count them. Read as bytes, as G5 reads
`buffer`, the same frames at `vec_int` (`frama-c-vec`, `cc-vec`), which WP
proves, are not true for an admitted call: that is G5's reading, and the
repair covers it.

**Decision (recommended).** The vec's mutable predicate, and the macro-body
`requires` that inlines it, gains
`\separated(v, v->items + (0 .. v->capacity - 1))`.

### G6 — bitset's single-bit residuals are false for a `Bitset` in its own words (opened)

**Finding.** In the x86_64 machdep WP uses, and with glibc on LP64, `u64`
and `usize` are the same C type, `unsigned long`, and share one memory
array in the model. With entry 3's placement,
`bitset_set`, `bitset_clear` and `bitset_toggle` store a word over
`word_count`: a same-type store, defined C, with no character write.
`bitset_set(bs, 0)` and `bitset_toggle(bs, 0)` leave `word_count` at 3,
and `bitset_clear(bs, 1)` at 0, and each one's `ensures bitset_mut(bs)` is
then false. Those three goals, `bitset_{set,clear,toggle}_live_ensures_4_part3`,
are residuals. VERIFY-020 files them in its single-bit family, under the
class it defines as "a true property the solver could not reach". They are
not
true for an admitted call: G5's shape, unproved and misfiled. The model
keeps the store and `word_count` in one array, so WP could not prove them,
and was right not to.

`bitset_assign` delegates to `bitset_set` and `bitset_clear`, and its live
`ensures bitset_mut(bs)` is not among the residuals: WP proves it from their
contracts. It is false whenever theirs is: proved, and false, because it
rests on residuals that are. `p_bitset_self.c`'s second part shows all
four, with both of `bitset_assign`'s branches, on LP64 Linux, sanitizers
clean. Where `u64` and `usize` are different types (ILP32; macOS, where
`u64` is `unsigned long long`), the compound assignment over `word_count`
reads it through `u64` before storing, which is undefined, and the part is
skipped.

**Repair.** Entry 3's: `bitset_mut` gains the separation. The prediction
for it will say which of the single-bit family's residuals close.

### G4 — listing, the rest of the survey

Every verified unit was read for the three kinds of pair G4's scope lists:
a character-type write (the `mem_*` functions, `memcpy`, `memset`,
`memmove`, `snprintf`, `vsnprintf`, and stores through `char`, `u8` or `i8`
lvalues) followed by a goal that reads another type; a write of any type
followed by a goal that reads the same bytes through a character type; and
writes and reads of signed and unsigned counterparts. For each write, every
goal evaluated after it that names an object it may overlap was checked.
Typed stores over an object of another, non-counterpart type in allocated
storage are G5's case, not G4's: the next read through the old type is
undefined. G5's case was not surveyed beyond `pool` and entry 5's `vec_int`
placements. Beyond entries 1 to 5:

- **Separated by a precondition or an invariant:** `stringbuf`
  (`stringbuf_wf`, and `sep` at `stringbuf_init_buffer`), the priority queue
  (`pq_wf`, and the separations of `out`), and `bitset_init`.
- **No goal after the write names another object:** `memory.h`'s
  primitives, the `u8` checked functions, `pool_alloc_zero`,
  `pool_try_alloc_zero`, `diag_render_frame` and `pq_peek`.
- **Disjoint by layout:** `diag_push`'s copies stay inside a frame's
  `message` array or the `frames` array, and `depth` lies outside both.
- **Counterparts:** the only pair in a verified unit is `vec_Rec`'s `i64`
  member against the vec's `usize` fields (`cc-vec_struct`), reached by the
  vec's own `usize` stores over a `Rec`'s `due` (entry 5).

The typed wrappers that `DEFINE_PRIORITY_QUEUE` generates are instantiated
in no verified unit. The listing's repairs follow G5's, one per prediction.

**Note (2026-10-18, at G18's score).** Since G18's repair (806bdeb)
`pool_alloc_zero` and `pool_try_alloc_zero` are not of the second group above.
`pool_alloc_zero`'s `alloc` postconditions read `*pool` and `*pool->arena`
after `mem_zero`'s write, kept off by `pool_invariant` and `arena_invariant`,
and `pool_try_alloc_zero`'s `zeroed` reads the slot's bytes through `char`
after the store through `out`, kept off by its new precondition. Both are of
the first group, and are filed in the proved-goal argument, rows 39 and 40.

### Protocol — the Linux runner pinned to `ubuntu-24.04` (committed prediction, before the pin commit)

**Decision (2026-10-09).** Every job that runs on `ubuntu-latest` moves to
`ubuntu-24.04`, in all six workflows. That covers each such `runs-on`, the
`ubuntu-latest` value of the three matrices that list it (`build`,
`static-analysis`, `lifetime-debug`) with their `include` and `exclude`
entries, and the three `matrix.os` conditions in `static-analysis`. The
`misra` job already runs on `ubuntu-24.04`. A note in
`cmake-multi-platform.yml`'s header says why, and each other workflow points
to it. No source, driver, pin or gate changes.

**Why now.** Every `ubuntu-latest` job of CI #1346 and #1347 carries
GitHub's notice that the label moves to Ubuntu 26 from 2026-10-19. The
announcement (actions/runner-images#14748) moves it from Ubuntu 24.04 to
26.04 between 2026-10-19 and 2026-11-19, and names `ubuntu-24.04` as the
way to stay. While a label migrates, the image it names can differ from
push to push and, since each job is given its own runner, between the jobs
of one run. The `misra` job met this, its count flipping between 780 and
1004 across pushes, and was pinned for it (its banner;
`docs/misra-campaign.md`). What the Frama-C jobs measure depends on the
image too. It supplies the gcc that preprocesses each unit, which the jobs
give no `-std`, and the system the cached opam switch is restored onto,
since the cache key names the runner only by `runner.os`. A pin that moved
during the migration could not be told apart from a change of image, and
the audit's next rounds fall inside it.

**Predicted: nothing moves.**

- (H) Every job of the CI and CC runs on the pin commit is green, and every
  proved line, count and roll-call is as it is now. Until 2026-10-19
  `ubuntu-latest` is Ubuntu 24.04, so the pinned label selects the image the
  jobs already run on, and the opam cache key, which names `runner.os`
  (`Linux` on both labels), restores the same switch.
- (H) The G4 probe runs, because its workflow file changes, and is green at
  its pinned `4 / 7`.
- (H) Record coverage runs, because its workflow file and
  `cmake-multi-platform.yml` change, and is green. Of the workflow it reads
  only the roll-call arrays.

`vc-identity` and `f4-control` run only on dispatch, so this push does not
exercise their pin. Job names that carry the matrix's `os` value change
(`build (ubuntu-24.04, …)` for `build (ubuntu-latest, …)`), and nothing in
the repository reads them. Required status checks in the repository's
settings, if any name these jobs, are outside the tree and would need
renaming by hand.

**What it settles.** From the pin commit on, the record's Linux
measurements are made on a fixed Ubuntu release, 24.04, not on a moving
label. The image's updates within 24.04 continue, as they have for every
run so far. Moving to 26.04 is a change of its own, to be predicted like any
other. The Windows and macOS jobs keep their `-latest` labels; none of them
runs Frama-C. The rows of `docs/traceability.md` that say `ubuntu-latest`
describe the runs they were measured on and stay as written.

### Protocol — the runner pin, scored (pin 25133fe; CI #1348, CC #35, G4 probe run #3)

**Result: exact on every scored part.** The pin commit changed no pin
(prediction 400da1d). Every job of CI #1348 and CC #35 was green, so every
unit's proved line, count and roll-call are as they were, by set equality.
The G4 probe ran, because its workflow file changed, and was green at its
pinned `4 / 7`. Record coverage #44 was green. GitHub's notice that
`ubuntu-latest` will migrate, which every `ubuntu-latest` job of CI #1346
and #1347 carried, appears on no job of these runs; the macOS jobs still
carry their notices about queue times. (GitHub's run pages, read
2026-10-09.)

**By part.**

1. Every CI and CC job green, every pin as it was (H): held.
2. The G4 probe re-runs green at `4 / 7` (H): held.
3. Record coverage green (H): held.

**A stated reason, not observed as stated.** The prediction expected the
opam cache to restore the same switch in every job. Three jobs took about
forty minutes longer than before: `frama-c-error` 43m 7s (1m 17s at
CI #1346), `frama-c-bitset` 2h 56m (2h 17m) and the G4 probe run 46m 50s
(4m 29s at run #2). Every other job took within a few minutes of what it
took before. Forty extra minutes is consistent with a cold build of the
switch after a missed cache restore; the job logs, which need a sign-in,
would say. If that is what happened, those three jobs built Frama-C and its
provers from the pinned versions and still met every pin, a harder test
than the prediction set.

### G5 — committed prediction for the repair (before the fix commit)

**Decision (2026-10-09).** The repair recommended with the finding, in
`core/pool.h`. `pool_init` gains a last precondition,
`requires \separated(pool, arena);`, so no clause is renumbered, and
`pool_invariant` gains the conjunct `\separated(p, p->arena)`. The header's
list of unsafe patterns says it for callers. No executable change. No other
verified unit includes `core/pool.h`, so only `frama-c-pool` can move. The
fix commit carries that job's predicted pins, as G2's and G3's did.

No WP run on the changed code precedes this prediction. The only local
check is a Frama-C 25.0 parse of `core/pool.h`.

**Predicted.** With the separation, a store into `*pool` no longer reaches
`*arena` in the model, and a call that assigns `*arena` no longer reaches the
`Pool`. Of the nine pool goals in the roll-call, seven close and two stay:

| # | Goal | Statement | Predicted | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `pool_init_ensures_2_part4` | `pool->used == 0` | closes | H |
| 2 | `pool_init_ensures_3_part4` | `pool->capacity == max_objects` | closes | H |
| 3 | `pool_init_ensures_4_part3` | on failure, `arena->offset == \old(arena->offset)` | closes | H |
| 4 | `pool_init_call_arena_alloc_requires` | `arena_invariant(arena)` after the four stores | closes | H |
| 5 | `pool_reset_call_arena_alloc_requires` | `arena_invariant(pool->arena)` after the store to `used` | closes | H |
| 6 | `pool_reset_reset_ensures_part3` | `pool->used == 0` | closes | H |
| 7 | `pool_reset_reset_ensures_2_part3` | `pool_invariant(pool)` after the reset | closes | M |
| 8 | `pool_init_ensures_part4` | `pool_invariant(pool)` on success | stays | M |
| 9 | `pool_reset_call_arena_reset_to_requires_2` | `pool->base_mark <= pool->arena->offset` | stays | H |

- Goals 1 to 3 and 6 ask only that a field the function stores, or one it
  must leave as it found it, survive stores into the other struct or a call
  that assigns `*arena`; goals 4 and 5, that `arena_invariant` survive the
  stores into `*pool`. With the separation each follows from hypotheses WP
  already has: the callees' `assigns` and postconditions, and
  `pool_invariant`'s new conjunct at `pool_reset`.
- Goal 7 re-establishes every conjunct of `pool_invariant` from the
  precondition. The `Pool`'s fields other than `used` are kept, the arena
  calls keep `buffer` and `capacity` (their frames) and re-establish
  `arena_invariant`, and the two separations carry over. M because it is
  the largest of the seven.
- Goal 8 also needs the conjunct `capacity <= CANON_USIZE_MAX / object_size`,
  which `pool_init` must derive from `checked_mul`'s `no_overflow`
  assumption, `aligned_size <= CANON_USIZE_MAX / max_objects`: the same bound
  read the other way, which takes nonlinear reasoning about integer division.
  Cat 2a's argument does not cover that conjunct. If goal 8 stays, its
  argument gains it: `aligned_size * max_objects <= CANON_USIZE_MAX`, so
  `max_objects <= CANON_USIZE_MAX / aligned_size`. M: the provers may
  manage it, and then this row misses in the good direction.
- Goal 9 asks for `base_mark <= arena->offset`, which `pool_invariant` does
  not state, and the separation does not bear on it. It is also not true for
  an admitted call: after `arena_reset` on the pool's arena, which the
  header lists as unsafe but no contract excludes, `pool_reset`'s call to
  `arena_reset_to` violates it whenever `base_mark > 0`. It stays, and is a

### G7 — `pool_reset` after its arena is reset (opened)

**Finding.** `pool_reset` requires `pool_invariant(pool)` and calls
`arena_reset_to(pool->arena, pool->base_mark)`, which requires
`mark <= arena->offset`. `pool_invariant` does not state that relation, and
the arena's own functions can break it while `pool_invariant` stays true:
`arena_reset` sets the offset to 0. The pool header lists resetting the
pool's arena while the pool is live as unsafe; no contract excludes it. The
call-site goal, `pool_reset_call_arena_reset_to_requires_2`, is pool
Cat 2d's last goal, filed under arena delegation. G5's prediction kept it
(H) and already noted that an admitted call falsifies it; it stayed. The
independent review of that prediction found the call sequence.

`tools/probes/verify-039/p_pool_reset_mark.c` takes one byte from the arena
before `pool_init`, so `base_mark` is 16, then resets the arena.
`pool_invariant` still holds, so `pool_reset` is admitted, and its call to
`arena_reset_to` has mark 16 and offset 0: the precondition is false. In the
proof configuration the call goes ahead and moves the offset forward; in the
default build `arena_reset_to`'s `require_msg` stops the program, the
run-time check catching the same false precondition. Both build
configurations, LP64 and ILP32, gcc and clang; the sanitizers are clean.

This is G1's shape again: a goal unproved because it is not true for an
admitted call, filed under an argument (delegation) that presumes the arena
was not reset under the pool.

**Repair (recommended).** `pool_invariant` gains
`p->base_mark <= p->arena->offset`. `pool_init` establishes it, since the
region starts `needed` bytes below the new offset. `pool_alloc` keeps it: it
touches no arena field, and G5 separates the two structs. `pool_reset`
re-establishes it: `arena_reset_to` sets the offset to `base_mark`, and
`arena_alloc` never lowers it. The goal then follows from the precondition.
A stronger conjunct, `end_mark <= arena->offset`, would state the header's
rule in full, the whole region reserved. But `pool_reset` can re-establish
it only if its `arena_alloc` provably succeeds, which needs the alignment of
`buffer + base_mark`, from which `arena_alloc` computes its pad; the
invariant does not state it, so it is left for later. With the weaker
conjunct, a rollback to or into the pool's region still meets the
contracts: `arena_reset` when the region starts at offset 0, or
`arena_reset_to` with a mark inside it. The header's unsafe patterns name
the first and not the second; the repair adds the second.

### G8 — `bitset_not`'s postcondition and loop invariant are false as written (opened)

**Finding.** `bitset_not`'s live behaviour ensures
`\forall integer k; 0 <= k < bs->word_count ==> bs->words[k] == ~\old(bs->words[k])`,
and its loop carries the same equation over the words already inverted, as
`loop invariant 2`. In ACSL the value of a C integer is promoted to a
mathematical integer, and `~` complements its infinite two's-complement
representation: `~x` is `-x - 1` (ACSL 1.18, §2.2.4 and §2.2.4.6, whose
Example 2.6 gives `~5 == -6`; Frama-C's E-ACSL plugin, run locally,
translates the term with GMP's `mpz_com`). For a `u64` word the right-hand
side is negative and the left-hand side is not. Every live call has at
least one word, so the postcondition is false for every call, and the
invariant at every loop head after the first.

Read as the comment above the loop intends, with the complement taken in
`u64`, the equation holds for every word but, possibly, the last. After the
loop `bitset_not` calls `bitset_clear_padding`, which clears the last word's
bits from `capacity % 64` up, so for a capacity that is not a multiple of 64
the last word is not the complement either, unless every padding bit was set
on entry, which `bitset_pad` excludes and the precondition, `bitset_mut`
alone, does not.
`tools/probes/verify-039/p_bitset_not.c` inverts a fresh `Bitset` of
capacity 100: word 0 is the complement, and word 1 is
`0x0000000fffffffff`, not `0xffffffffffffffff`, `VIOLATED`. At capacity 128
both words hold. Both build configurations, LP64 and ILP32, gcc and clang at
`-O0` and `-O2`; the sanitizers are clean.

**Filing.** The invariant's preservation,
`bitset_not_loop_invariant_2_preserved`, is a residual, and VERIFY-020
files it as array framing ("array framing on and / or / xor / not";
`data/bitset.h`'s comment glosses it "writing words[w] leaves words[0..w-1]
alone"). It is unproved because it is false. The postcondition is not among the
residuals: WP proves it. A false goal can be proved only from a false
hypothesis, and for an ordinary `Bitset` the only one WP has there is the
invariant, which WP assumes at the loop's exit, where it states that a word
equals a negative number. Every goal after the loop has that hypothesis, so
its proof says nothing about whether it is true. VERIFY-020 counts the
postcondition among what contracting the loop delivered ("6 → 3 with both
postconditions proved"); it was never true. The other one,
`ensures bitset_pad(bs)`, also follows from `bitset_clear_padding`'s
postcondition, and nothing here says it needed the contradiction.

This is G1's shape twice over: a residual unproved because it is false,
filed as prover weakness, and a proved goal that rests on it, as at G6.

**Repair (recommended).** Both clauses take the complement in `u64`. The
postcondition states it for every word but the last, and for the last, when
`capacity % 64 != 0`, the complement with the bits from `capacity % 64` up
cleared, and otherwise the complement. That needs `bitset_clear_padding` to
state what it leaves in the last word; today it states only `bitset_pad`.
With entry 3's separation, in the bitset repair.

### G6 — the single-bit padding postconditions are false too

**Finding.** G6 showed `bitset_set`, `bitset_clear` and `bitset_toggle`'s
`ensures bitset_mut(bs)` false on LP64 for a `Bitset` whose `word_count` is
its own first word. Their `ensures bitset_pad(bs)`,
`bitset_{set,clear,toggle}_live_ensures_3_part3`, residuals in VERIFY-020's
single-bit family too, are false for an admitted call as well.
`p_bitset_self.c`'s third part starts the words at the `Bitset`'s
`capacity`, 97, so that `words[1]` is `word_count`, 2. `bitset_mut` and
`bitset_pad` hold: `2 >> 33` is 0. `bitset_clear(bs, 5)` and
`bitset_toggle(bs, 5)` clear bit 5 of the capacity, which becomes 65:
`bitset_mut` still holds, two words for 65 bits, and `bitset_pad` is
`VIOLATED`, `2 >> 1` being 1. `bitset_set(bs, 64)` sets bit 0 of
`word_count`, which becomes 3; the padding test then reads the word past the
`Bitset`, all ones, and is `VIOLATED`, as is `bitset_mut`. LP64 Linux, both
build configurations, gcc and clang; the sanitizers are clean. The part is
skipped where `u64` and `usize` differ, as the second part is.

VERIFY-020 files the three as true properties the solver could not reach.
Like the `bitset_mut` goals, they were not true for an admitted call. The
repair is entry 3's.

### G4 — listing entry 3 and G6, committed prediction for the repair (before the fix commit)

**Decision (2026-10-10).** The repair recommended with entry 3, in
`data/bitset.h`: `bitset_mut` gains a last conjunct,
`\separated(bs, bs->words + (0 .. bs->word_count - 1))`, which
`bitset_init` already requires. The `Bitset`'s documentation says it for
callers. No executable change. G8's repair, `bitset_not`'s clauses, is not
part of this one, so that each can be read from its own run. `bitset.h` is
verified in `frama-c-bitset` alone, and only bitset's own goals can move.

No WP run on the changed code precedes this prediction. The local checks
are a Frama-C 25.0 parse of `vmacros/vdrivers/bitset_verify.h`, the same
version's RTE annotation of it, to number the memory-access assertions, and
the C probes. WP's source was read for its loop rule (`cfgCalculus.ml`,
`cfgWP.ml`). An independent review of a first draft, which predicted 29
closures, found that ten of them rest on a loop rule WP does not have; this
version predicts 19.

**The reading behind it.** In the x86_64 machdep WP uses, a `u64` word and
the `Bitset`'s `capacity` and `word_count` (`usize`) are the same C type,
`unsigned long`, and share one memory array in the model. Without the
separation a store to a word may land on either field, so no fact about the
fields survives a word store, and G6 shows that such stores happen for
admitted calls. Bitset's own residuals follow that line: after a word
store, the goals that need `capacity` or `word_count` to keep their values
are residuals, and those that do not are proved. The boundary runs through
single functions:

- The single-bit postconditions about the bit and about the other words
  prove; those about `bitset_pad` and `bitset_mut`, which need the fields
  unchanged, do not.
- In `bitset_clear_padding` only the path with the store has residuals. On
  the other nothing is written: the frame and `bitset_mut` are the
  precondition's, and `bitset_pad` holds by its first disjunct.
- `bitset_or`'s loop assigns `words[0 .. n - 1]`, with `n` a local, and
  `or` has no assigns residual. `bitset_and`'s second loop assigns
  `words[n .. bs->word_count - 1]`, and `bitset_xor` calls
  `bitset_clear_padding`, whose `assigns` names `bs->word_count`; each has
  one.
- `bitset_and`'s memory-access assertion 11, the second loop's store,
  bounded by `bs->word_count`, is a residual; assertion 5, the first loop's
  store, bounded by `n`, proves. (Numbered by the local Frama-C 25 RTE run;
  10 and 12 there are the reads of `&bs->word_count` and `&bs->words`, which
  `\valid_read(bs)` covers.)

With the separation a word store with an index below the old `word_count`
misses the `Bitset`. That covers the single-bit stores, whose index the
unit's proved memory-access assertions already bound, `bitset_clear_padding`'s
store, and every loop whose assigns region is bounded by `n`, which is fixed
at entry and at most the old `word_count`. It does not cover a loop whose
assigns region is bounded by `bs->word_count` itself. WP takes a loop's
`assigns` in the loop's current, havocked state (`cfgWP.ml`: `cc_assigned`,
`LoopAssigns -> s1`, for the havoc and the check against the function's
`assigns`; `cc_effect`, `LoopAssigns -> env`, for the body's writes), so a
`word_count` that has grown in that state widens the region over a `Bitset`
lying past its words, which the separation, stated over the words as they
were, does not exclude. In that model state `bitset_and`'s second-loop
store can zero `word_count`.

**Predicted to close: 19.**

|---|---|---|
| `bitset_{set,clear,toggle}_live_ensures_4_part3`, `ensures bitset_mut(bs)`, G6's goals | 3 | M |
| `bitset_clear_padding_ensures_2_part1` (the frame) and `_ensures_3_part1` (`bitset_mut`) | 2 | M |
| `bitset_and`, first loop and the second loop's entry: `loop_invariant_2_preserved_part1`, `_part2`; `loop_invariant_3_established_part1`, `_part2` | 4 | M |
| `bitset_or`: `live_ensures_part3`, `_part4`; `loop_invariant_2_preserved_part1`, `_part2` | 4 | M |
| `bitset_xor`: `call_bitset_clear_padding_requires_part1`, `_part2`; `live_assigns_normal_part5`, `_part6`; `loop_invariant_2_preserved_part1`, `_part2` | 6 | M |

**Predicted to stay: the other 52 of bitset's own residuals, and every
inherited one.**

- The ten goals of the two loops whose assigns are bounded by
  `bs->word_count`:
  - (H) `bitset_and`'s `loop_invariant_3_preserved_part1`, `_part2` and
    `live_assigns_part5`, `_part6`, and `bitset_not_live_assigns_exit_part1`

### G8 — committed prediction for the repair (before the fix commit)

**Decision (2026-10-11).** The repair recommended with the finding, in
`data/bitset.h`:

- `bitset_not`'s loop invariant 2 and postcondition take the complement in
  `u64`: `(u64)~\at(bs->words[k], Pre)`. The postcondition states it for
  every word but the last in one clause, and the last word in two: the
  complement when `capacity % 64 == 0`, and otherwise the complement and
  the mask of the bits below `capacity % 64`. `ensures bitset_pad(bs)`
  stays.
- `bitset_clear_padding` gains the two matching clauses, its last word
  unchanged or masked. Its three clauses stay.
- The mask is written with the code's casts,
  `(u64)((u64)((u64)1 << (usize)(bs->capacity % 64)) - 1)`. They change no
  value for `capacity % 64` from 1 to 63, and they make WP's translation of
  the clause the code's own. Written plainly,
  `((u64)1 << (capacity % 64)) - 1`, the store path's clause in
  `bitset_clear_padding` asks the provers to show that the shifted value
  stays below 2^64, bit-level reasoning of the kind bits.h's residuals
  record them not reaching.

No executable change; only `frama-c-bitset` can move.

**The probe.** `tools/probes/verify-039/p_bitset_not.c` now checks the
repaired clauses of both functions too, at eight capacities from 1 to 129
and three patterns, one with every padding bit set, which `bitset_pad`
excludes and the precondition admits. They hold in all 48 checks, 24 cases
for each function. The old postcondition read in `u64` is `VIOLATED` for
the last word in 11 of the 24, holding at 64 and 128 and wherever every
padding bit was set (at 63 the mixed pattern's one padding bit is), as G8
says. gcc and clang, `-O0` and `-O2`, both build configurations, LP64 and
ILP32; the sanitizers are clean. The probe now exits 0: its status counts
the repaired clauses only.

**Before the prediction.** No external prover has been run on the changed
code. As for the loop bounds, WP 25.0-beta, built locally, printed the
unit's goals with CI's options less the provers, plus `-c11`; printing runs
Qed. The mask's form was chosen from those statements: in the plain form
the store path's clause keeps the shift, and in the cast form it reduces to
the code's own term. With the change WP 25 generates 4852 goals, against
4842: ten new, all in `bitset_clear_padding` and `bitset_not`. Outside
those two functions, three goals change in statement, call-effect `assigns`
goals of `bitset_set_all` and `bitset_xor`, which gain the new clauses
among their hypotheses.

**Reading.**

- Invariant 2 in `u64` is true, and its preservation needs neither the
  frame nor the separation: the store writes the complement of the word
  that the third invariant, at the current head, says is the word on entry,
  and leaves the others. G8's residual closes.
- G8's invariant was contradictory at the next loop head, at the loop's
  exit, where the count is at least 1, and at the current head after the
  first iteration; with the repair it is a fact. At ecb3c0d eleven proved
  goals of `bitset_not` had it among their hypotheses: the first
  postcondition, restated below, and ten others. Two of the ten do not

  (WP 25's `assert_rte_mem_access_2` and `_6`). The proofs of the other
  eight could stand on its contradiction, and now need one of their own:
  - the counter's bound and the frame of the words not yet inverted
    (`loop_invariant_preserved`, `loop_invariant_3_preserved`) and the

    A store reaching `word_count` would find it, by that invariant, at its

  - the store's validity (WP 25's `assert_rte_mem_access_3`), the loop's

- `bitset_clear_padding`'s new clauses, on the path with the store, need

- `bitset_not`'s new clauses follow from `bitset_clear_padding`'s,

### G4 — listing, entry 6: `remove`'s `out` over the `vec_Rec`

**Finding.** `remove` requires `out` to be valid and, since G1, separated
from the vec's buffer. Nothing separates it from `*v`, and entry 5's repair
does not: it keeps the vec off its buffer. In `cc-vec_struct`, on LP64, a
`Rec` at the vec's own address has its `id` over the vec's `items` field,
its padding over the rest of that field, and its `due` over `len`: an `i64`
over a `usize`, signed and unsigned counterparts, which the model keeps in
two arrays. `remove` stores the removed element through `out` and then reads
`v->len`, which now holds the element's `due`. When that makes
`i < v->len - 1` false, `remove` skips the move, reads `v->items` no more,
and stores `v->len - 1` over `out->due`. Two goals that WP proves are then
false:

| Goal | Statement | After `p_vec_rec_out.c`'s call |
|---|---|---|
| `vec_Rec_remove_ok_ensures_2` | `*out == \old(v->items[i])` | `*out` is `{2, 0}`; the element was `{2, 1}` |
| `vec_Rec_remove_ok_ensures_3` | `v->len == \old(v->len) - 1` | `len` is 0, not 2 |

`tools/probes/verify-039/p_vec_rec_out.c` calls `remove(v, 2, out)` at `len`
3, the element's `due` 1, with `out` at the vec and the buffer a separate
block, so the call meets `remove`'s contract, before entry 5's repair and
after it. No part of either clause is among `cc-vec_struct`'s residuals. In
WP 25's statements of the path without the move (`_part7`), the element's
`due` lies in the `sint64` array and `len` in the `uint64` one: the store to
`len` leaves `*out` as stored, and the store through `out` leaves `len`.

Every access is defined C, on the reading of C11 6.5p6 and 6.5p7 that entry
5 uses, in which each member of a stored `Rec` takes its own effective type.
Both blocks are heap storage. `remove` reads `v->len` after the store
through `out`, a counterpart read, and `v->items` only before it. The probe
reads `out->id` through its own type, `out->due` as an `i64`, the
counterpart of the `usize` stored there last, and through `memcpy`, and
`v->len` through its own type. It does not read `v->items`, whose bytes now
hold `out`'s `id` and padding: ensures 4 and 5 read it, and that read is the
undefined step of G4's scope. gcc and clang at `-O0`, `-O2` and
`-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3`, both build configurations; the sanitizers are clean.
On ILP32 `due` covers `len` and `capacity`, two four-byte `usize` fields,
and the probe says so.

No other vec function has such a goal. At `vec_int` (`frama-c-vec`,
`cc-vec`), on LP64, an `out` over the vec stores an `int` over its pointer
or `usize` fields, and the next read of that field through its own type is
undefined: G5's case. (On ILP32, where `usize` is `unsigned int`, an `int`
over `len` would be a counterpart store; no unit verifies vec there.) `pop`
stores `len` and `*out` in one expression, `*out = v->items[--v->len]`, so
an `out` over `len` makes two unsequenced stores to the same bytes, which is
undefined (C11 6.5p2), and `iter_next` does the same with the iterator's
index. After `get`'s and `iter_next`'s stores, their goals read the vec's
`items` field, overwritten when `out` lies on it, and are true when `out`
lies past it.

G1's score says that the frames it closed proved with no argument once the
contract was true. That stands for those frames, but the contract G1 left
still admits this call, for which `remove`'s ensures 2 and 3 are false.

**The survey.** Its counterparts bullet named one route to this pair, the
vec's own `usize` stores over a `Rec`'s `due`: entry 5. This is the other, a
`Rec` stored through `out` over the vec's `len`. The survey states that for
each write it checked every goal evaluated after it that names an object the
write may overlap. For this write it did not: it took `out` as unable to
overlap `*v`, which G1 separates from the buffer only. The other
out-parameters in verified units give no further pair: deque's store an
`int`, no counterpart of a `usize` on LP64, and the priority queue's are
separated from the queue or followed by no goal that names it. The survey's
list of pairs stands; its entries for this pair are 5 and 6.

**Decision (recommended).** `remove`'s `out` is separated from the vec as
well as from its buffer, within G1's guard: `\separated(out, v)`. `pop`'s,
`get`'s and `iter_next`'s go with it (`iter_next`'s from the iterator and
its vec), so the four functions G1 changed keep one shape. In both contract
surfaces, as at G1. One intervention per prediction: after entry 5's.

### G4 — the proved goals whose evidence is an argument: how they are filed (decision and method)

**What is to be filed.** WP's typed model keeps one memory array per integer
kind and per character type, so a write through one is never seen through
another. C sees it in two cases (G4, scope): through a character type, and
through the signed or unsigned counterpart. A goal WP proves across such a
write takes from the model that the write left the location the goal reads
alone; the proof does not show that it did, and the evidence is an argument.
The listing's six entries were the 23 library goals for which nothing kept
the write off: false for an admitted call, and true now by the separations
the repairs added. The other goals that cross such a write are, on the
survey's reading, true all along, kept apart by a precondition, an
invariant, the code's index ranges or layout, and their evidence is the same
kind of argument. G4's plan (G4, opened) files all of them under one stated
hypothesis, each read against the write's range, VERIFY-017's and MCDC-009's
readings of `diag_push` included. But for the 23, held so in prose, the
record still treats every proved goal as needing no argument.

**Decision (recommended).** One block, a `**Proved-goal argument**`, states
the hypothesis once and lists the properties it covers, by unit, function
and clause, each with the write it crosses and the fact that keeps the write
off what the property reads. A property is filed when, after such a write,
it reads a location of another type, or a typed object's bytes through a
character type, or a counterpart, and its proof takes from the model that
the write left that location alone. A property proved from a filed one
through a callee's contract, at the call (the callee's precondition) or
after it (its postcondition), is not filed again: WP's modular proof carries
the filed property's truth to it, as it carries any proved contract's. A
property with a part among CI's residuals is filed for its other parts.
`tools/record_coverage.py` will check that no filed part becomes a residual,
since a filed goal that stops proving needs a residual argument instead.

The block is the counterpart, for proved goals, of a residual's argument
block. It is not counted in *A*, which counts the arguments that cover
residual obligations (the paper's §2). The record reports it beside *A*, as
it reports trusted axioms (VERIFY-031), with its numbers of properties, of
write sites and of the facts that keep a write off, since each fact is a
reason a reviewer reads. The paper's reading of *A* as the size of the
unverified human evidence (§2, §5) then holds for the residue only, and its
next revision says so.

**Method.** WP 25, printed with the goal names as for entries 5 and 6, gives
for each unit (every verified unit but `frama-c-arena-32`, which verifies
`frama-c-arena`'s functions at the 32-bit machdep) the goals evaluated after
a call to a named byte-level writer: `mem_copy`, `mem_move`, `mem_zero`,
`mem_set`, `mem_secure_zero`, `mem_swap`, `mem_swap_buf`, `mem_copy_bytes`,
`mem_move_bytes`, `mem_zero_bytes`, `mem_set_bytes`,
`mem_secure_zero_bytes`, `memcpy`, `memmove`, `memset`, `snprintf` and
`vsnprintf`. Properties are named by WP's property prefix, without `_partk`,
since WP 25's parts can differ from CI's. Less the pinned residuals, that
list has 157 properties in 28 functions at f74e95a:

|---|---|
| `core/memory.h`, in the ten units here that include it and `frama-c-arena-32` | `mem_swap` (8), `mem_swap_buf` (6), `mem_zero` (1), `mem_secure_zero_bytes` (1) |
| `core/arena.h`, seven units here and `frama-c-arena-32` | `arena_alloc_zero` (4), `arena_alloc_aligned_zero` (4), `arena_reset_secure` (6) |

### G4 — the proved-goal argument

**Proved-goal argument**: WP's typed model keeps one memory array per
integer kind, `char`'s and `unsigned char`'s among them, and one for
pointers. A write through one array leaves the others unchanged in the
model; in C it changes every byte it covers, whatever type reads them next.
Each property below reads, after a write through one array, locations in
another that the write would change if its range covered them: after a
character-type write, a location of another type; after a store of another
type, bytes through a character type; after an integer store, a location
through the signed or unsigned counterpart of the stored type. WP takes
those locations to be unchanged. The hypothesis is that they are: that the
write's range and the locations read are disjoint. Each row gives the write
and its range, what the property reads after it, and the fact that keeps the
two apart; the facts are stated once, below. Where the fact holds, so does
the hypothesis, and the property is true, as WP proves it. Its evidence is
that argument, not the proof alone: without the fact the proof stands and
the property can be false, as the goals G4 found were before its repairs.

The facts that keep a write off what a property reads:

- **F1** — `arena_invariant(a)`, since G4 entry 1's repair (7e5757f):
  `\separated(a, a->buffer + (0 .. a->capacity - 1))`. A write inside the
  buffer leaves `*a` alone.
- **F2** — `pool_invariant(p)`, since G4 entry 2's repair (f3d9520):
  `\separated(p, p->arena->buffer + (p->base_mark .. p->end_mark - 1))`. A
  write inside the slots leaves `*p` alone.
- **F3** — `bitset_mut(bs)`, since G4 entry 3's repair (27e24f9):
  `\separated(bs, bs->words + (0 .. bs->word_count - 1))`. A write inside
  the words leaves `*bs` alone.
- **F4** — `bitset_init`'s precondition, since its first contract (f42841c):
  `\separated(bs, words + (0 .. bitset_words_for(capacity) - 1))`.
- **F5** — `Diag`'s layout: the overflow shift's destination,
  `(DIAG_MAX_FRAMES - 1) * sizeof(DiagFrame)` bytes from `&d->frames[0]`, is
  `frames[0 .. DIAG_MAX_FRAMES - 2]`, and `depth` lies after
  `frames[DIAG_MAX_FRAMES - 1]`.
- **F6** — `DiagFrame`'s layout and the copy's bound: the loop invariant
  `copy_len_bounds` keeps `len <= DIAG_MAX_MSG_LEN - 1`, so the copy and its
  `'\0'` stay inside the pushed frame's `message`, a member of its own;
  `depth`, that frame's other members and the other frames lie outside it.
- **F7** — `diag_render`'s `r_sep`, since G4 entry 4's repair (838a204):
  `\separated(buf + (0 .. buf_size - 1), d)`.
- **F8** — `stringbuf_wf(sb)`, since `stringbuf.h`'s first contracts
  (f6e54ca, VERIFY-031):
  `\separated(sb, sb->data + (0 .. sb->capacity - 1))`. A write inside the
  buffer leaves `*sb` alone, and a store to `*sb` leaves the buffer's bytes
  alone.
- **F9** — `stringbuf_init_arena`'s precondition `sep_storage`, since
  f6e54ca:
  `\separated(sb, ((char *)arena->buffer) + (arena->offset .. arena->capacity - 1))`,
  the arena's free tail at entry.
- **F10** — `stringbuf_init_buffer`'s precondition `sep`, since f6e54ca:
  `\separated(sb, buffer + (0 .. cap - 1))`.
- **F11** —
  `\separated(pq, (char*)pq->data + (0 .. pq->capacity * pq->elem_size - 1))`,
  in `pq_wf` and in `pq_init`'s matching precondition since VERIFY-022's run
  4 (b79a51f), and in `pq_wf_buf`, which `pq_wf` includes and `pq_heapify`'s
  `live` behaviour requires, since run 5 (5173cd2). A write inside the
  buffer leaves `*pq` alone.
- **F12** — `pq_pop_raw`'s `nonempty_out` precondition, since VERIFY-022's
  run 5 (5173cd2):
  `\separated((char*)out + (0 .. pq->elem_size - 1), pq, (char*)pq->data + (0 .. pq->capacity * pq->elem_size - 1))`.
  The copy into `out` leaves `*pq` alone.
- **F13** — the vec's mutable form, since G4 entry 5's repair (66b54e0):
  `\separated(v, v->items + (0 .. v->capacity - 1))`, in `vec_int_mut`
  (`frama-c-vec`) and in the first `requires` of the fourteen macro-body
  contracts (`cc-vec`, `cc-vec_struct`). A write inside the buffer leaves
  `*v` alone, and a store to `*v` leaves the elements alone.
- **F14** — the precondition G1's repair (40cccd9) gave `get`, `pop` and
  `remove`:
  `(v != \null && out != \null) ==> \separated(out, v->items + (0 .. v->capacity - 1))`,
  and `iter_next` over `it->vec`. A write inside the buffer leaves `*out`
  alone.
- **F15** — the conjuncts G4 entry 6's repair (f74e95a) added to the same
  clause: `\separated(out, v)`, and in `iter_next`
  `\separated(out, it) && \separated(out, it->vec)`. The store through `out`
  leaves `*v` and `*it` alone, and their stores leave `*out` alone.
- **F16** — the ranges of vec's byte-level writes, by the code:
  `append_array`'s copy writes `items + (len .. len + count - 1)`,
  `insert`'s move `items + (i + 1 .. len)` and `remove`'s
  `items + (i .. len - 2)`. None reaches an element below `len` at the copy
  or below `i` at a move, the elements the frames keep, nor, at the copy, one
  from `len + count` on, which `append_array`'s fifth postcondition keeps
  since VERIFY-040 round 2.
- **F17** — `pool_try_alloc_zero`'s precondition on the slot it hands out,
  since G18's repair (806bdeb): when `out` is not null and
  `pool->used < pool->capacity`, `out` is separated from the slot, the
  `object_size` bytes at
  `pool->arena->buffer + pool->base_mark + pool->used * pool->object_size`.
  The store through `out` leaves the slot's bytes alone.

### G4 — the proved-goal argument, group A: `memory.h`, `arena.h`, `pool.h`

The filing goes by header, not by unit, since a header's goals recur in
every unit that includes it.

**Candidates.** The decision's larger list (no simplification; after a named
writer or a function whose `assigns` writes a character range) has 66
properties in these headers: 43 in `memory.h`, 17 in `arena.h` and 6 in
`pool.h`. Reading the three headers adds 10 the search did not list:

- `pool_try_alloc_zero`'s 3 at or after its call to `pool_alloc_zero`, whose
  `assigns` writes the slots through `char *`. The search's list of such
  functions missed `pool_alloc_zero`, `pool_try_alloc_zero` and
  `pool_reset_secure`; of the three only `pool_alloc_zero` has a caller in
  the verified units, `pool_try_alloc_zero`.
- `mem_secure_zero`'s 7 at or after its loop's store `p[i] = 0` through
  `volatile u8 *`, the one character-type store in the three headers: the
  preservation of the loop invariant, the variant's two goals, the loop
  `assigns`, the store's `mem_access` and the two behaviours' `assigns`.

Neither of the decision's last two kinds gives a candidate. No goal reads
bytes through a character type after a store of another type: the only goals
in the three headers that read bytes after a store are `mem_zero`'s
`zeroed`, of the bytes `memset` wrote through `char`, and the two zeroing
allocators' `ensures_3`, through `u8` after a `char` write: on the path
through `mem_zero` (`_part1`) G3's residuals, unproved, filed in
VERIFY-009's category 2c; on the other (`_part2`) `\result` is null and
nothing is read. Apart from the writers' character ranges and that loop, the
headers store only into `Arena` and `Pool` fields and through `out`
parameters, each through its declared type, so no counterpart pair arises.

**Filed: 10**, the block's rows 1 to 4. Seven are entry 1's arena
postconditions. The other three are `pool_reset_secure`'s: the precondition
at its second call to `pool_reset`, made after the zeroing, and its two
`assigns` properties, whose parts for that call check its effect,
`*(pool->arena)` in `pool_reset`'s `assigns`, and so read `pool->arena`
after the write and take it to be unchanged.

**Not filed: 66.**

| Why not | Properties |
|---|---|
| `assigns`, whose effects after the write, if any, are at addresses computed from parameters and locals; the clause's locations are taken in the pre-state | 26 in `memory.h`; `arena_alloc_zero`'s and `arena_alloc_aligned_zero`'s `assigns_normal`; `arena_reset_secure`'s `assigns_normal` and `null_or_empty_assigns_normal`; `pool_alloc_zero`'s `assigns_normal`; `pool_try_alloc_zero`'s `assigns_exit` and `assigns_normal`; `mem_secure_zero`'s loop `assigns` and its two behaviours' `assigns` (36) |
| validity and separation, of the allocation and of addresses, not of memory | the 12 `memcpy` preconditions in `mem_swap` and `mem_swap_buf`; the two zeroing allocators' `ensures_2` (`\valid`); `arena_reset_secure`'s `mem_access_4` and `_5`, at its stores after the write; `pool_try_alloc_zero`'s `mem_access`, at `*out`; `mem_secure_zero`'s `mem_access` (18) |
| values and the loop index | `mem_copy_bytes`'s and `mem_move_bytes`'s four `\result` postconditions; the preservation of `mem_secure_zero`'s loop invariant and its variant's two goals (7) |
| the written bytes, read through the write's type | `mem_zero`'s `zeroed`, from `memset`'s contract (1) |
| locations stored after the write | `arena_reset_secure`'s `non_empty` `ensures` and `ensures_2`, `offset == 0` and `padding_accum == 0` (2) |
| dependents, through `pool_reset`'s postconditions | `pool_reset_secure`'s `secure_ensures` and `secure_ensures_2` (2) |

The two dependents read `pool->arena` at the call too, through the guard of
`pool_reset`'s `reset` behaviour, `pool->arena != \null`. They stay
dependents because the guard follows from the filed precondition there:
`pool_invariant` gives `\valid(p->arena)`. The two `assigns` properties need
`pool->arena` at the call to equal its value at the function's entry, which
no filed goal gives.

**Goals the entries missed.** Entry 1 listed `pool_reset_secure`'s
`ensures pool_invariant(pool)` (`secure_ensures_2`), and entry 2 the same
goal. Under the decision's rules it is a dependent: WP proves it from
`pool_reset`'s postcondition, and the goal it rests on, which crosses the
write, is `pool_reset`'s precondition at the call,
`call_pool_reset_2_requires`. That goal was proved and false for the same
admitted calls, and neither entry named it, nor two more goals of the same
function:

- the other dependent, `secure_ensures` (`pool->used == 0`), false for a
  third placement. `tools/probes/verify-039/p_pool_reset_call.c` observes
  the state at the call on entry to `pool_reset`, through
  `-finstrument-functions`, and finds `pool_invariant` false there in
  `p_pool_self.c`'s two placements and in a third: the `Pool` over the end
  of slot 0, so that the zeroing nulls `pool->arena` but not `used`.
  `pool_reset` then returns at once, and `used` stays 1.
- `assigns_normal`, false for a fourth, which an independent review of this
  commit found (`tools/probes/verify-039/p_pool_reset_assigns.c`).
  `pool_invariant` makes neither the slots' start, `buffer + base_mark`, nor
  `object_size` a multiple of a pointer's alignment. `pool_init` does both,
  since `arena_alloc` aligns the address it returns and `mem_align` the
  size, but the contract admits a `Pool` whose fields are set otherwise.
  With the `Pool` at slot 0 of one-byte slots and `used` 1, the zeroing
  clears one byte, `pool->arena`'s first (its low byte on the project's
  little-endian targets), and turns it into the address of another `Arena`,
  64 bytes before the real one in the same heap block. `pool_reset` then
  resets and re-reserves that `Arena`, which `pool_reset_secure`'s `assigns`
  does not name. Both postconditions hold there.

Nor were these all. The entries named the goals their probes falsified, not
every goal of the same functions that an admitted placement falsifies, and a
review of this commit found one more in entry 4's function: `diag_render`'s
`loop_variant_decrease`, proved in `frama-c-diag`. With `buf` from the last
frame's message to `depth`'s second byte, `snprintf` truncates frame 0's
line there: a message byte `0x05` lands on `depth`'s low byte and the `'\0'`
on the next, so `depth` goes from 2 to 5 and the variant `d->depth - i` from
2 to 4 at the first back edge. The loop renders frames 1 to 4 with nothing
left to write and exits, `render_i_bounds` holding throughout
(`tools/probes/verify-039/p_diag_variant.c`). Entry 4's `r_sep` makes it
true now; the `diag.h` filing files it.

**The count.** The library goals G4 has found proved and false are therefore
27, not 23. Of them, 24 fall under the block's rules: the decision's 22 with
`call_pool_reset_2_requires` in place of `secure_ensures_2`,
`assigns_normal`, and `diag_render`'s variant; 9 of them are filed here. The
other 3 are dependents: `bitset_set_all`'s `ensures bitset_mut(bs)` and
`pool_reset_secure`'s two postconditions. The decision's "17 the named-call
list has" counted a dependent; with the precondition in its place the count
is unchanged. Each goal the six entries named was proved and false, and
their statements stand; all 27 are true now by an argument. Each header's
filing checks the goals it files, and their dependents, against the
placements the repairs excluded. For group A that is done: of the 10 filed,
9 were false, entry 1's seven, the precondition and `assigns_normal`;
`assigns_exit` was not shown false, as in the proof configuration nothing on
its path exits; both dependents were false.

**Record coverage.** `tools/record_coverage.py` now reads the block, taking
properties from each row's Properties cell and facts from its "Kept off by"
cell. For each filed property it reports a pinned residual whose name is the
property's or one of its `_partk`, unless the row excludes that part, since
a filed goal that stops proving needs a residual argument instead. It also
reports a property filed twice, an excluded part no longer pinned, a fact
stated but not cited, and any problem reading the block: a row whose cells
differ in number from the header's, one not numbered or before the header,
one with no property or no fact, a name outside backticks, a property whose
name lacks its row's function, a fact cited but not stated, or counts that
differ from the block's closing line. A name misspelled after its function's
part is not caught, since the script has the pinned names, not WP's whole
list. It is advisory, like the rest of the script; `--strict` fails on a
pinned filed part or a problem reading the block. At this commit it reports
4 write sites, 10 properties and 2 facts, nothing pinned and no problem.

**Names and units.** The properties are named from WP 25's prints. WP 29
names its goals by the same scheme, property and part, and the two differ in
how a property splits into parts (entries 5 and 6), so the check works by
prefix. `frama-c-arena-32` is not run here; its Gate D holds its residuals
to the 64-bit set by name, so the arena rows' properties are proved there
too.

### G4 — the proved-goal argument, group B: `bitset.h`, `diag.h`

**Candidates.** The decision's larger list has 65 properties in these
headers: 12 in `bitset.h` (`bitset_clear_all` 2, `bitset_init` 3,
`bitset_set_all` 7) and 53 in `diag.h` (`diag_init` 2, `diag_push` 39,
`diag_render` 5, `diag_render_frame` 7). Reading the headers adds 40 the
search did not list, of four kinds:

- goals after a store through `char`, which is not a call: `diag_render`'s
  and `diag_render_frame`'s `buf[0] = '\0'`, each ahead of a guard and a
  `snprintf`;
- goals inside or after a loop whose body writes through `char`. In such a
  goal the earlier iterations' writes are the loop's `assigns`, taken at the
  head, not a call, so the search cannot see them. The decision did not name
  this kind. `diag_render`'s loop calls `snprintf` once per frame, so every
  goal in its body, and after it, reads memory that earlier iterations may
  have written;
- `assigns_exit` goals that check a writer's own effect at its exit, which
  the print marks `(* Exit '...' *)`, a marker the search did not match;
- goals WP prints without a path, as `Prove: true`, that follow a write in
  the code.

They are 23 in `diag_render` (its goals after the store that the list does
not have), 12 in `diag_render_frame` (its seven field reads, its two
`snprintf` preconditions and its three `assigns_exit`), three at a writer's
exit (`diag_init`'s `assigns_exit`, and `bitset_clear_all`'s
`live_assigns_exit` and `null_assigns_exit`), and two printed without a
path, after `diag_push`'s shift (its `loop_assigns`, and
`assert_rte_mem_access_5`, the dead clamp's store). That makes 105
candidates. With exit markers matched too, the search lists 483 properties
in 46 functions. The 54 it adds are all `assigns_exit`: 23 in group A's
headers, 9 here and 22 in `stringbuf.h` and `priority_queue.h`.

Neither of the decision's last two kinds gives a candidate. `diag.h` reads
through a character type only bytes it wrote that way, or `msg`, which
`push_no_alias` keeps off `*d`. `bitset.h` stores `u64` words; on LP64 that
is the C type of `capacity` and `word_count`, so WP sees such a store
through either field (G6's residuals), and on ILP32 the sizes differ, so
there is no counterpart.

**Filed: 38**, the block's rows 5 to 11.

  entry 3's; `bitset_set_all`'s two `assigns` properties, whose parts for

- `diag_push`, rows 8 and 9: on the overflow path every goal after the shift

that lands on `bs->words` or `word_count` turns it into all ones, and

precondition like `diag_render`'s `r_sep` would close that; it is a contract
change, for a prediction of its own.

**Dependents through a loop invariant.** The decision does not file again a
property proved from a filed one through a callee's contract, since WP's
modular proof carries the filed property's truth to it. A loop invariant
does the same within a function: WP proves it established and preserved, and
assumes it at each head. In these loops, the goals in the body before the
call that read `*pq`, the postcondition at the exit, and `pq_sift_down_`'s
variant positivity, which WP checks at the end of an iteration on the value
at its head, read `*pq` in the state of a head, with no write between, and
need of it only what the invariants state there: `pq_wf(pq)` and
`idx < pq->len`, or in `pq_heapify` `pq->len == n`. WP's model also lets
such a goal use the precondition, taking the fields at the head to be those
at entry, but the goal is true wherever the invariants are, and their
preservation is filed (`idx < pq->len` in rows 21 and 22, `pq->len == n` in
row 23) or a dependent (`pq_wf`, through `pq_swap_`'s and `pq_sift_down_`'s
postconditions). These goals are dependents too. A goal that needs a field
the invariants do not restate is filed, as `pq_heapify`'s first
postcondition needs `capacity`.

**Decision (recommended).** Each obligation is filed by name under the one
argument that covers it, read against its code.

- The filing is a goal table in this record: a line
  `**Filed by name**: VERIFY-nnn, <heading>`, citing a counted block in
  force by its record and the start of its heading, up to the colon or the
  count (`VERIFY-008, Category 1`), and under it a table, with nothing but
  blank lines between, each row numbered and giving one goal as pinned, the
  units that pin it, and what reading it against the code found. A batch
  writes a table for each block it files under, so a block may collect
  tables from several batches. The cited block's argument then covers the
  goal as it covers its own table's.
- An obligation no counted block's argument covers gets a block of its own,
  a `**Manual proof argument**` with its goal table, and *A* counts it,
  cumulative and in force; any batch may so move *A*. The paper's claim that
  the budget saturated, Δ*A* = 0 over its last seven units, is then tested
  by explicit filings, not assumed.
- An obligation found false for an admitted call becomes a gap of this
  record, predicted and repaired as G1 was.
- 38 of the primitives' 44 are argued in the module-level prose of
  VERIFY-002 to VERIFY-007, which the paper's operational count leaves out
  (§2; Table 1's note), and ptr.h's six in VERIFY-027's, as above. Filed by
  name, each goes under a counted block whose argument covers it, or its
  prose becomes a block: the batch says which, and what that does to *A*.
- A goal is filed once, and filing it under a block reads that block's
  argument against the goal's code.

**Method.** Six batches, each a commit that accounts for its obligations,
filed or found false:

1. vec, 50 at `int` (`frama-c-vec`, `cc-vec`) and 50 at `Rec`
   (`cc-vec_struct`), VERIFY-018 and VERIFY-037/038;

**Record coverage** reads the tables. Each goal filed by name counts for the
cited block as its own table's goals do: it must be pinned somewhere, it is
reported stale if not, and it leaves the count of pinned names in no goal
table. A block's heading count is checked against the distinct goals of its
own table, or, for one with none, against those filed by name under it; a
batch that files under such a block restates the count in its heading, as
batch 4 will for option's and result's if the fresh instantiations go under
them. A block's own table is read from its heading to its argument, the
filing tables there left out, so a block written below a filing table under
the same heading does not take in its rows. A retired block covers nothing:
it keeps rows only for goals that closed, and a goal still pinned in its
table counts as in no goal table. The Units cell is checked against the
units that pin the goal as the gates pin it, `frama-c-checked`'s two named
goals and the priority queue's run-time pin of memory.h's names included;
`frama-c-arena-32`, whose copy of arena's list the script does not read, may
be named beside `frama-c-arena`. Filing problems are a line that starts
`**Filed by name`, indented or not, but does not read as one from its first
column; a citation that matches no block, several or a retired one; a line
with no table after it, or a table with no row read; a row not read, as one
not numbered or whose goal cell holds other than one goal in backticks; a
Units cell that differs from the pins; a goal filed twice; and a goal still
pinned in a retired block's table. `--strict` fails on them, and the summary
line counts them. A new option, `--complete`, fails while a pinned name is
in no goal table. The job runs advisory; its comment, which says to promote
it to `--strict` once option, result, borrow and diag list their goals by
name, is corrected when it is promoted to `--strict --complete` at the
pass's end: a change to a workflow file runs the whole CI matrix, which a
comment alone does not warrant. No table is written yet, so the report is as
before but for its wording, the summary's count of filing problems, and its
counts by unit, which now include those two pins: 394 pinned names in no
goal table, the 392 obligations and bits.h's two sample names. The main pass
ends when that count is 0 and the open items are settled. Every residual
obligation pinned is then filed by name under exactly one block in force,
which the script checks; whether each filing is sound remains a human
judgment, as the paper's §2 says.

  unprovable by construction, no annotation surviving in a macro body;

The headings say 5 for (d) and 22 for (h); 3 and 21 are live.

**The standard.** A goal is filed under a block when it fails for the
mechanism the block's argument addresses, and the argument's reasoning, with
the premises the row reads at the goal's site, shows it true. diag.h's
argument is written for its own sites; its root cause states its class, the
Typed+Cast gap between byte ranges and typed locations, and names memory.h's
`mem_copy` and `mem_move` among the class's sites. Its reasoning is what
vec's 42 need: the bytes of a valid typed range are valid and lie in its
footprint, and a byte copy of whole objects copies the objects. Its own
eight goals are given their table in VERIFY-017 here, read against diag.h's
code, so that its heading counts its own goals and vec's stand beside them:
diag.h's part of batch 5 is done here, and batch 5 keeps borrow's block and
arena Cat 2c.

Each row's premises hold under the first precondition (`len <= capacity`,
`items[0 .. capacity - 1]` valid, `*v` outside it: F13), on the branch the
call is on and, for `append_array`, under its `ok` preconditions; the ranges
written are F16's. At these calls the pointers are not null, and the size is
positive but for `append_array` with `count` 0, where its rows hold
trivially; so `mem_copy` and `mem_move` reach `memcpy` and `memmove`. The
`assigns_exit` parts are the same effects on a path that would end in
`exit`, and nothing on these paths exits. At `Rec` the bytes include each
element's padding, which the copy and the move carry along, and the
postconditions compare the fields.

`append_array`'s fourth postcondition reads `src[k]` after the store to
`len`, and until G9's repair no clause separated `src` from `*v`. On LP64 a
`src` over the vec's fields would read their bytes as `int`, or as a `Rec`
whose `id` lies on a pointer or a `usize`, which C leaves undefined (C11
6.5p7): no call on which the postcondition's reads are defined makes it
false there, and at `Rec` none does on ILP32 either. At `int` on ILP32,
`usize` is `unsigned int`, an `int` read of `len` is a counterpart read, and
a call falsified it: G9. Since the repair (1d725ef) the contract keeps `src`
off `*v` as off the buffer, so neither the copy nor the store to `len`
writes `src`'s elements, and the postcondition holds for every admitted
call.
