#### A call through the formatting callback, a pointer no clause can list (1)

| # | Goal | Units | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `typed_cast_vec_int_to_stringbuf_cb_assert_rte_function_pointer` | `frama-c-vec-fmt` | `\valid_function(cb)` before the call `cb(sb, items[i])` |

**Functions affected**: `vec_int_to_stringbuf_cb` (`frama-c-vec-fmt`).

**Root cause**: the callback form calls the caller's formatter through the
pointer `cb`, which is arbitrary by design, so no `calls` clause can list it.
The contract requires `\valid_function(cb)` wherever the call is made (its
`cb_ok`), and WP 29 does not implement `\valid_function`: it turns the
run-time check into `false`, which no prover discharges where the context is
consistent. Verifier-bound: a WP that implemented `\valid_function` would
prove it from the precondition.

**Manual proof argument**: The call is made only past the guard
`if (!v || !sb || !cb)` and the empty vector's return, so where it is made
`v`, `sb` and `cb` are not null and the length read at entry is positive.
That is the condition under which `cb_ok` requires `\valid_function(cb)`.
`cb` is a parameter, not changed by the function. A callback cannot reach it,
since its address is never taken. So at every call, in every iteration,
`cb` is the pointer the precondition holds valid, and the check holds for
every call the contract admits. This is VERIFY-014's argument for option's
checks, and VERIFY-015's for result's, at another family.

**Retirement.** A WP that implements `\valid_function` (the case of option's,
result's and the queue's checks), or a formatter mechanism whose formatters
are listed, so that `calls` names them.

#### The callback loop's own state across a call through an unlisted pointer (3)

| # | Goal | Units | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `typed_cast_vec_int_to_stringbuf_cb_loop_invariant_preserved` | `frama-c-vec-fmt` | `0 <= i <= n` after an iteration |
| 2 | `typed_cast_vec_int_to_stringbuf_cb_loop_variant_decrease` | `frama-c-vec-fmt` | `n - i` decreases across an iteration |
| 3 | `typed_cast_vec_int_to_stringbuf_cb_assert_rte_mem_access_3` | `frama-c-vec-fmt` | `items[i]` is readable at the call's argument |

**Functions affected**: `vec_int_to_stringbuf_cb` (`frama-c-vec-fmt`).

**Root cause**: across a call through a pointer with no `calls` clause, WP 29
takes the call to write everything and keeps only validity, which its model
of the call does not free (VERIFY-039 G19). The loop states no frame, since
none can be checked against such a call without `region_end`'s
`for no_hook:` device. So after a call, nothing ties the counter `i`, the
length `n` and the buffer `items` read at entry to their values before it.
The invariant's preservation, the variant's decrease and the access
`items[i]`, which needs `i < n` and `items` as at entry, stay unproved. These
are `region_end`'s two loop goals under VERIFY-011's Category 1, and an access
of the same kind. Verifier-bound: the facts lost are about locals, which C
puts out of any callee's reach.

**Manual proof argument**: `i`, `n` and `items` are locals of
`vec_int_to_stringbuf_cb` whose addresses are never taken. A callee can reach
an object only through a pointer to it or through its own scope, so no
callback can write them; `n` and `items` are also `const`. Across each call
they therefore keep their values: `n` and `items` are the length and buffer
read at entry, and `i` is the iteration's index. The loop condition gives
`i < n` before the call, and the increment makes `i + 1 <= n` after it, so
`0 <= i <= n` is preserved: goal 1. `n - i` falls by one each iteration and
stays non-negative: goal 2. At the head, `i < n` and `items` is the buffer the
precondition `v_ok` holds readable for `n` elements, and a callback frees
nothing in WP's model and, by the contract's `v_ok`, has no license to free
in C. So `items[i]` is readable: goal 3. Each holds for every call the
contract admits.

**Retirement.** A WP that keeps unaddressed locals across a call through an
unlisted pointer, or a `calls` clause that can name the formatter, which
would give the call a frame. Neither is an admissible change of
`vec_fmt.h`: a callback is arbitrary by design (the record's P1).

**What this does to *A*.** Two blocks are written at module 21, both
verifier-bound and both needed, as P1 predicted: *A* is 33 cumulative and 19
in force, and *V* 21 and 16. The paper's Table 1 is frozen at module 19 and
does not change.

### Closed (2026-10-28)

**Run 3** is 270494a, at CI #1389. Every job is green, `frama-c-vec-fmt`
among them, with its gates: `5239 / 5286`, zero Failed or Invalid, the count
47 and the roll-call. Record coverage #115 passes with no name pending. Run
3's three predictions match.

| # | verdict |
|---|---------|
| P1 | **MATCH** — two blocks, both needed and verifier-bound, for exactly P6's four goals. |
| P2 | **MATCH** — 43 names, in both runs and at enforcement. |
| P3 | **MATCH** — all three, `fmt_ok` (L) included. |
| P4, P7, P8 | **MATCH** |
| P5 | **MATCH** (L) |
| P6 | **MATCH** — the predicted kinds, `items[i]`'s access as the second review added. |
| P9 | recorded: both needed blocks are about an indirect call to unknown code, catalogued kinds, neither n(*P*)'s one new kind. An instance against the by-kind form, exploratory, carrying nothing. |

**What module 21 adds to Table 1.** 4 own distinct obligations; 2 blocks
written, both needed (*V*). It is the fourth unit verified under a
prediction committed before any contract. It is the first whose prediction

kind and the goals. A unit that calls code no contract can describe needs an
argument for what the verifier loses at that call. VERIFY-040's verdict on
the queue's comparator says the same, and so does `region_end`'s hooks'.
`vec_fmt.h` adds two more instances, at another family. The two reviews
mattered: the first draft predicted one block and one goal, and three of the

## VERIFY-044: Pre-registration — C23: Canon-C Did Not Compile Under the Current Standard

| Field          | Value |
|----------------|-------|
| **ID**         | VERIFY-044 |
| **Date**       | 2026-10-29 |
| **Status**     | PREDICTED — this record is committed before the fix commit, which is pushed with it; both before any CI run of either |
| **Baseline**   | 873ed2e (CI #1390) |
| **Scope**      | `core/primitives/contract.h`, eight `CANON_RESULT(bool, Error)` instantiations and the comments that explained their name, `CMakeLists.txt` (the standard made overridable), `test/core/primitives/contract_test.c`, the `misra` job's expected-count text, and a CI job `c-standards` (C11, C17 and C23, GCC 14 and clang 18, Debug with sanitizers) |
| **Category**   | Portability defect in the shipped headers, found by a compile check while weighing the platform additions; an API addition decided with the author |

**Why this record exists.** The README says "Requires C99 or later". The CI
pins C99 in `CMakeLists.txt`, so nothing built under a later standard. C23
is the current standard, and GCC 15 compiles as `gnu23` by default. A check
made on 2026-10-28, compiling every test file with `gcc-14 -std=c23` and the
project's warning flags, found **48 of 56 failing**. C11 and C17 compile
cleanly.

### Findings

**C1 — `bool` is a keyword in C23, so the result type's name changes.**
`CANON_RESULT(bool, Error)` builds names by token pasting. In C99 to C17,
`bool` is a macro for `_Bool`, and the name is `result__Bool_Error`, the name
every container's functions are written against (the headers' comments say
so). In C23, `bool` is a keyword. It is not expanded before `##`, so the
pasted name changes and every use of `result__Bool_Error` fails: unknown
type names and undeclared functions, the bulk of the 48 failures. Eight
instantiations are affected:
- `util/log/log.h`;
- `algo/fold/fold_impl.h` and `fold_decl.h`;
- `data/deque/deque_impl.h`;
- `data/priority_queue.h`;
- `data/hashmap/hashmap_decl.h` and `hashmap_impl.h`;
- `data/vec/vec_impl.h`.

**Fix**: write `CANON_RESULT(_Bool, Error)`. `_Bool` is a keyword in every
standard from C99 to C23 and is pasted as written. The name is
`result__Bool_Error` everywhere, and in C99 to C17 the expansion is token
for token the one `bool` produced.

**C2 — `unreachable` is a standard macro in C23.** C23's `<stddef.h>`
defines `unreachable()`, a hint whose reaching is undefined behaviour.
`contract.h` defines its own `unreachable()`, which calls the contract
handler in debug builds and under `CANON_STRICT`. Under C23 the two clash,
and `-Werror` reports "unreachable redefined" in every test file. Redefining
a standard library macro is undefined behaviour in ISO C (7.1.3), so
Canon-C cannot keep its definition under that name in C23.

**Fix, decided with the author on 2026-10-29** (options: a new name with
the old one kept where it can be; override the standard macro; rename and
drop the old name):
- `canon_unreachable()` carries Canon-C's semantics in every standard.
- `contract.h` includes `<stddef.h>`. If the standard library does not
  define `unreachable`, `unreachable()` is `canon_unreachable()`, as before.
  If it does (C23), `unreachable()` is the standard's, and the header says
  so.
- Nothing changes before C23. `unreachable_msg()` has no standard
  counterpart and keeps its name.

**C3 — the build could not be asked for another standard.**
`CMakeLists.txt` sets `CMAKE_C_STANDARD 99` unconditionally, so
`-DCMAKE_C_STANDARD=23` is ignored, silently: the compiler still gets
`-std=c99` (checked in `flags.make`). **Fix**: set 99 only when no standard
is given.

**C4 — the Release test executed a hint whose reaching is undefined.**
Found while changing `contract_test`. In Release without `CANON_STRICT`,
`unreachable()` and `unreachable_msg()` expand to
`__builtin_unreachable()`. The test ran both inside `FIRES(...)` and
expected no handler call, so every Release leg executed undefined
behaviour and passed by the compiler's choice. **Fix**: in that
configuration the macros are compiled behind a branch never taken
(a `volatile` flag) and not executed. They are still executed, and must
fire, in Debug and under `CANON_STRICT`.

### Measured before this record, locally

A first pass, in a scratch copy, with C1's fix, C3's, and a first form of
C2's (the standard macro kept under C23, with no `canon_unreachable` yet),
built the suite with GCC 14 and clang 18, Debug, ASan and UBSan:
- under C99, C11 and C17: 55 of 55, both compilers;
- under C23: 54 of 55 with both. The failure was `contract_test`, whose test
  of `unreachable()` expects the handler to fire, and under C23 that is the
  standard's macro, which never does.

That failure is what made C2's API decision necessary, and the fix's test
changes answer it. `contract_test` tests `canon_unreachable()` in every
standard. It tests `unreachable()` as Canon-C's only where the header says
it is (`CANON_UNREACHABLE_IS_CANON`). It never executes the standard's
macro, whose reaching is undefined.

Then the fix itself, as committed after this record:
- **Tests**: 55 of 55 under C99, C11, C17 and C23, each with GCC 14 and
  clang 18, Debug with ASan and UBSan; and under C99 and C23 in Release,
  both compilers. Every `flags.make` carried the requested standard (GCC
  14's C23 flag, under CMake 3.28, is spelled `-std=c2x`).
  `CANON_UNREACHABLE_IS_CANON` is defined under C99 and not under C23.
- **C99 identity for WP**: every file a WP job is run on (21 headers and
  drivers) was normalised by Frama-C (`-print`, local WP 25, the shared
  include and define flags), under both `-C` and `-CC`, before and after:
  42 of 42 identical. With GCC, `-E -P` of the 15 drivers is identical
  too. Under `-CC`, GCC's output gains only its `<stddef.h>` licence
  comment, from the new include, whose code is already guarded out.
- **MISRA**: the `misra` job's command, run on the baseline and on the
  fix, gives **54 → 55**. The count was 54 on the baseline, so the scan
  reproduces CI's. The change is the scanner, not the code. cppcheck does
  not read system headers (`missingIncludeSystem` is suppressed), so it
  never saw `<stdbool.h>` and pasted `bool` as written. That gave it
  `result_bool_Error`, which collided with `fold.h`'s compatibility macros
  of that name: rule 5.5 at `log.h` and `fold_impl.h`. With `_Bool` it
  sees the compiler's names:
  - the two 5.5 go;
  - rule 19.2, the result union, appears at `fold_impl.h`, the one
    instantiation without the inline MISRA-DEV-014 suppression every
    other carries. The fix adds it (33 → 34 inline sites);
  - rule 5.7 appears at the same two lines: the tag `result__Bool_Error`
    is defined in several headers, under one guard, as at
    `fold_decl.h:59` already;
  - rule 2.3 appears at `fold.h:164`: the `result_bool_Error` typedef
    is unused in the header.

  The three new findings are reported, not deviated here. cppcheck
  reports one finding per location, so suppressing a finding can expose
  another one at the same line, as the 19.2 suppression exposed 5.7. The
  job's expected-count text is updated.

### The CI job

`c-standards`: `ubuntu-24.04`, a matrix of `c_std` ∈ {11, 17, 23} and
`c_compiler` ∈ {gcc-14, clang}, each configured with
`-DCMAKE_C_STANDARD=${c_std}`, Debug, sanitizers on, and `ctest
--no-tests=error`. C99 stays the default everywhere else.

### Predictions

| # | prediction | falsified if | confidence |
|---|------------|--------------|------------|
| S1 | `c-standards` passes in all six legs: 55 of 55 under C11, C17 and C23, GCC 14 and clang 18, with no sanitizer report. | any leg fails | H for C11 and C17; M–H for C23 (only the first form of C2's fix was run locally) |
| S2 | Under C99 the WP surface does not change: every proved line, `EXPECTED_UNPROVED` and roll-call holds, in every Frama-C job. | any of them moves | H (normalised ASTs identical, above) |
| S3 | `misra` prints 55 real findings: the 54 less the two 5.5, plus the two 5.7 and the 2.3 above. | another count, or another composition | H (the job's command, run here; cppcheck 2.13.0 locally, as the runner's) |
| S4 | `coverage`'s MC/DC figures hold. | any figure moves | M (not run locally; the test change adds executions, in `test/`, whose macro-body conditions the job filters) |
| S5 | Every other job is green, Release legs included: `contract_test` no longer executes the hint (C4). | any red | H |

The fix is pushed with this record, in the commit after it. Its hash
follows this one, and neither has run in CI.

### Scored (2026-10-29)

CI on 21506e4 is green, the author reports. The fix commit landed as
21506e4 and the record as 45b8811: `git am` re-created the commits, so their
hashes differ from the ones in the patches. The author pasted the
`c-standards` logs and the `misra` summary.

The `c-standards` logs show the standard check passing in all six legs:
`55 -std=c11` twice, `55 -std=c17` twice, `55 -std=c2x` (GCC 14's spelling)
and `55 -std=c23`. All 55 targets built in each. The pasted text does not
include the Test step's output. Each leg passed, and its `ctest` runs with
`--no-tests=error`, so a leg that found no test would have failed.

| # | verdict |
|---|---------|
| S1 | **MATCH**. All six legs pass. |
| S2 | **MATCH**. Every Frama-C job is green. The enforced jobs fail on a moved proved line, unproved set or roll-call. |
| S3 | **MATCH on the count**. `Real violations: 55`, canary 3. The composition (two 5.5 gone; two 5.7 and one 2.3 new) was predicted from the local scan, which gave the same count. The CI report artifact was not read, so the composition is matched locally, not in CI. |
| S4 | **NOT ESTABLISHED**. `coverage` is green, but the job enforces only its branch-coverage threshold, not the MC/DC figures, and its log was not read. It stays open until the figures are read. |
| S5 | **MATCH**. Every other job is green, the Release legs among them, where `contract_test` no longer executes the hint. |

**Status**: C1 to C4 are fixed. Canon-C now builds and passes under C11,
C17 and C23, with GCC 14 and clang 18, and CI holds it there. S4 stays open
until the coverage figures are read.

## VERIFY-045: Pre-registration — Big-Endian: the First Byte-Order Target

| Field          | Value |
|----------------|-------|
| **ID**         | VERIFY-045 |
| **Date**       | 2026-10-29 |
| **Status**     | PREDICTED — this record is committed before the fix commit, which is pushed with it; both before any CI run of either |
| **Baseline**   | 1a3a9f0 |
| **Scope**      | `test/data/bitset_test.c`, `test/semantics/option_test.c`, `data/bitset.h` (documentation only, no ACSL), and a CI job `big-endian` (Linux s390x, GCC cross-compiled, tests run under qemu-user, Release and Debug) |
| **Category**   | Portability: one test defect observed on the new target, one found by inspection, and an undocumented byte-order property of a public view |

**Why this record exists.** Every target in the matrix is little-endian:
x86-64, i386 (`-m32`), AArch64 Linux and macOS, and Windows. Code that
reads a multi-byte object as bytes has run in only one byte order. s390x is
big-endian with 64-bit pointers. Ubuntu 24.04 packages a cross-compiler for
it (`gcc-s390x-linux-gnu`, GCC 13.3) and `qemu-user`, so the suite can run
on a standard runner. This is the second of the platform additions decided
on 2026-10-28.

### Findings

**B1 — `bitset_as_bytes`'s byte order was undocumented, and its test
assumed little-endian.** The view is the u64 words' object representation,
so which byte holds a given bit depends on the host's byte order. The
header did not say so, and offered the view "for I/O and serialization".
Bytes written on a host of one byte order and read on the other are a
different bitset. `test_as_bytes` asserted the little-endian layout
(`bv.ptr[0] == 1` after setting bit 0; `bv.ptr[7] == 0x80` after bit 63).
On s390x both assertions fail: observed locally, in Debug and Release.
- **The code is right; the documentation and the test were not.** A view
  must not reorder bytes, and an O(1) view cannot.
- **Fix:**
  - The header states the byte order, says where bit i sits in each byte
    order, and drops "serialization".
  - The test derives the expected byte indices from a probe of the host's
    byte order. It also checks that the view's bytes equal the words',
    which is the documented property, in either order.
- A portable, byte-order-independent export is not added here. That would
  be an API decision.

**B2 — `option_test` compared padding.** `test_none_value_zero_initialized`
`memcmp`'d two whole `option_int` objects. `{ bool has_value; int value; }`
has padding after `has_value`, whose bytes are unspecified, so the
comparison held by chance. Found by inspection while weighing this target;
**not observed failing**, on s390x or anywhere. **Fix**: compare
`has_value`, and check that `value`'s bytes are zero in each.

### Measured before this record, locally

- **s390x baseline** (1a3a9f0, `s390x-linux-gnu-gcc` 13.3, `qemu-s390x`
  8.2.2): 54 of 55 in Debug and in Release. `bitset_test` fails at its
  lines 418 and 421, B1's two assertions. Nothing else fails.
- **With the fix**: 55 of 55 on s390x, Debug and Release. On x86-64, 55 of
  55 with GCC and clang, in Debug with sanitizers and in Release. The
  binaries are `ELF 64-bit MSB ... IBM S/390`.
- **WP**: `bitset.h` changes only in comments outside ACSL. Frama-C's
  normalised AST of `bitset_verify.h` (local WP 25) is identical before and
  after, under `-C` and `-CC`.

### The CI job

`big-endian`: `ubuntu-24.04`, a matrix of Release and Debug.
- It installs `gcc-s390x-linux-gnu`, `libc6-dev-s390x-cross` and
  `qemu-user`.
- It cross-configures CMake for `s390x` and sets
  `CMAKE_CROSSCOMPILING_EMULATOR` to `qemu-s390x -L /usr/s390x-linux-gnu`,
  so CTest runs each test under qemu.
- It checks that `bitset_test` is an MSB S/390 binary, then runs `ctest
  --no-tests=error`.
- No sanitizers: their runtimes are not reliable under qemu-user.

### Predictions

| # | prediction | falsified if | confidence |
|---|------------|--------------|------------|
| E1 | `big-endian` passes in both legs: 55 of 55, binaries MSB S/390. | either leg fails | H (measured locally, same Ubuntu packages) |
| E2 | Nothing else moves. Every Frama-C pin holds, `misra` prints 55 (it does not scan `test/`, and `bitset.h` changes only in comments), and every other job is green. | any pin, the count, or any other job moves | H |

VERIFY-044's S4 (the MC/DC figures) stays open until the coverage figures
are read. This record does not touch it.

The fix is pushed with this record, in the commit after it. Its hash
follows this one, and neither has run in CI.

### Scored (2026-10-29)

CI #1392 (62da0d2) is green in every job, the author reports. That
includes `Canon-C CC` #64. The record landed as f799b2d. The author pasted
the `coverage` job's MC/DC table.

| # | verdict |
|---|---------|
| E1 | **MATCH**. Both `big-endian` legs pass. A leg fails if its binaries are not MSB S/390, or if `ctest` finds no test. Their logs were not read. |
| E2 | **MATCH for the pins and the jobs**: every enforced Frama-C job is green, and every other job too. **`misra`'s count was not read** (the job is advisory and passes at any count). |

**VERIFY-044 S4 closed: MATCH.** CI #1392 runs VERIFY-044's code and
VERIFY-045's. VERIFY-045 changes only `test/` (filtered from the tables)
and comments. Its coverage job gives the same three totals as CI #1388,

- MC/DC 1932 / 2096, 164 missed;
- branches 1717 / 1872;
- lines 2796 / 2883.

A move in one file offset by another would not show in a total. The

- `priority_queue.h` 81/82;
- `range.h` 61/62;

- `vec_cover.c` 155/158;

- the two 5.5 gone.

## VERIFY-046: Pre-registration — Bare-Metal Arm: a Compile Check for the README's Embedded Claims

| Field          | Value |
|----------------|-------|
| **ID**         | VERIFY-046 |
| **Date**       | 2026-10-29 |
| **Status**     | PREDICTED — this record is committed before the fix commit, which is pushed with it; both before any CI run of either |
| **Baseline**   | 459c6e6 |
| **Scope**      | `semantics/error.h` (`error_in_range`'s body; the contract unchanged), `test/data/priority_queue_test.c`, `README.md` (the bare-metal section), a script `tools/embedded_compile_check.sh`, and a CI job `embedded` |
| **Category**   | Portability defect in a shipped header, found by a compile check; one test defect it had masked; a documentation gap |

**Why this record exists.** The README's bare-metal section makes specific
claims:
- Tier 0 and Tier 1 headers work on any 32-bit-or-wider target, given a
  replaced contract handler.
- stdio is inert on newlib or picolibc stubs.
- malloc is reached only through `mem_alloc` and `data/convenience/`.

No job compiled anything for such a target. `arm-none-eabi-gcc` with newlib
is the common bare-metal toolchain. It differs from every hosted target in
the matrix in two ways that matter to C code:
- enums are short (`-fshort-enums` is its ABI default);
- newlib's `int32_t` is `long`, not `int`.

This is the third of the platform additions decided on 2026-10-28.

**What the check is, and is not.** It compiles every public header as its
own translation unit, and every test file, under the project's warning
flags (C99, `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`). It does this for Cortex-M0+
and Cortex-M4 (hard float), at `-O0`, `-Os` and `-O2`. **Nothing is
linked or run.** The check shows that the code compiles cleanly there. It
does not show that the code works there. Left out, each for a stated reason
(the script lists them):
- `util/time.h` and its test need an OS clock (A3).
- The concurrency test needs pthreads.
- `*_impl.h` and `*_mangle.h` are template fragments, reached through the
  headers that include them.
- The five hashmap headers that need `HASHMAP_KEY_TYPE` are compiled
  through `hashmap_test.c`.

### Findings

**A1 — `error_in_range` did not compile under `-Werror` with short enums.**
With `-fshort-enums`, `Error` is `unsigned char`, and GCC's `-Wtype-limits`
reports `(int)e >= (int)ERR_OK` as always true. Every translation unit
that includes `semantics/error.h` failed:
- `error.h` itself, the containers, `diag`, `log`, `parse`, `file`,
  `fold`;
- 21 of the 79 header units and 17 of the 54 tests, at every CPU and
  level: 95 of 133 compiled.

All 38 failures have this as their first error (measured on the
baseline). **Fix**: the value goes through a local `int`, so the comparison
no longer appears to be on a narrow type. The contract is unchanged.
- **WP** (local WP 25, Z3): `error.h`'s per-property goal counts are
  identical before and after. 57 of 57 locally, where CI's pin is 65 of 65
  with three provers.
- **MISRA**: the first form of the fix added a rule 12.1 at that line, a
  rule held at zero. The committed form is parenthesised, and the local
  scan gives the same 55 findings as CI #1392's report, line for line.

**A2 — `priority_queue_test`'s comparators returned `i32`.**
`algo_cmp_fn` returns `int`. On every hosted target `i32` is `int`, so
this went unseen. On arm-none-eabi it is `long`, and passing the
comparators is an incompatible-pointer error. It was masked by A1, since
the test includes `error.h`, and surfaced once A1 was fixed. **Fix**: they
return `int`. The library's own comparators already did; the header sweep
passes.

**A3 — the README's bare-metal section counted two platform dependencies;
there are three.** It named stdio and malloc. `util/time.h` also needs a
monotonic OS clock (`QueryPerformanceCounter` or
`clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)`), and newlib on bare metal has neither, so
the header does not compile there. The section's own Tier 2 paragraph
lists "OS clocks", so the tiers were right and the summary was not.
**Fix**: the section names the clock, and says what CI checks and what it
does not.

### Measured before this record, locally

`arm-none-eabi-gcc` 13.2.1 (Ubuntu 24.04's `gcc-arm-none-eabi`), newlib
4.4.0:
- **Baseline**: 95 of 133 at each of the six configurations, all 38
  failures A1's.
- **With the fix**: 133 of 133 at all six, in 81 seconds.
- **Hosts**: 55 of 55 with GCC and clang, Debug with sanitizers, and under
  C23 with clang.

### The CI job

`embedded`: `ubuntu-24.04`. It installs `gcc-arm-none-eabi` and
`libnewlib-arm-none-eabi`, then runs `tools/embedded_compile_check.sh`.
The script fails on any failed compile, or if either list is empty.

### Predictions

|---|------------|--------------|------------|
| A-P1 | `embedded` passes: 133 of 133 at all six configurations. | any compile fails | H (same Ubuntu packages, measured) |
| A-P2 | `frama-c-error` holds its pins: 65 / 65, nothing unproved, roll-call unchanged. | any moves | H (per-property counts identical locally) |
| A-P3 | `misra` prints 55, with CI #1392's findings. | another count or composition | H (local scan, line for line) |
| A-P4 | Every other job is green. | any red | H |

The fix is pushed with this record, in the commit after it. Its hash
follows this one, and neither has run in CI.
